questions.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $53u+12v=\text{gcd}(53,12).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}53 & = & 12\cdot 4 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 12 & = & 5\cdot 2 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(12,53)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =53-12\cdot 4 \\ 2 & =12-5\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =5-2\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-2\cdot 2 \\  & =5-[12-5\cdot 2]\cdot 2 \\  & =5\cdot 5-12\cdot 2 \\  & =[53-12\cdot 4]\cdot 5-12\cdot 2 \\  & =53\cdot 5-12\cdot 22 \\  & =53\cdot 5+12\cdot (-22)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=5$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=5+(-22)=-17.
$$

questions.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $69u+30v=\text{gcd}(69,30).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}69 & = & 30\cdot 2 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 30 & = & 9\cdot 3 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 3\cdot 3 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(69,30)=3.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =69-30\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =30-9\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =30-9\cdot 3 \\  & =30-(69-30\cdot 2)\cdot 3 \\  & =30\cdot 7-69\cdot 3 \\  & =69\cdot (-3)+30\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$

questions.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $86u+35v=\text{gcd}(86,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}86 & = & 35\cdot 2 & + & 16 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 16\cdot 2 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 16 & = & 3\cdot 5 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(86,35)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}16 & =86-35\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =35-16\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =16-3\cdot 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =16-3\cdot 5 \\  & =16-[35-16\cdot 2]\cdot 5 \\  & =16\cdot 11-35\cdot 5 \\  & =[86-35\cdot 2]\cdot 11-35\cdot 5 \\  & =86\cdot 11-35\cdot 27 \\  & =86\cdot 11+35\cdot (-27)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=11$ and $v=-27.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=11+(-27)=-16.
$$

questions.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $80u+35v=\text{gcd}(80,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}80 & = & 35\cdot 2 & + & 10 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 10\cdot 3 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 10 & = & 5\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(80,35)=5.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =80-35\cdot 2 \\ 5 & =35-10\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =35-10\cdot 3 \\  & =35-[80-35\cdot 2]\cdot 3 \\  & =35\cdot 7-80\cdot 3 \\  & =80\cdot (-3)+35\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$

questions.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $71u+29v=\text{gcd}(71,29).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}71 & = & 29\cdot 2 & + & 13 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 29 & = & 13\cdot 2 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 13 & = & 3\cdot 4 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

  

As a result, $\text{gcd}(71,29)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =71-29\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =29-13\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =13-3\cdot 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =13-3\cdot 4 \\  & =13-[29-13\cdot 2]\cdot 4 \\  & =13\cdot 9-29\cdot 4 \\  & =[71-29\cdot 2]\cdot 9-29\cdot 4 \\  & =71\cdot 9-29\cdot 22 \\  & =71\cdot 9+29\cdot (-22)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=9+(-22)=-13.
$$
